task.description: Independently review this diff against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8, with particular attention to REQ-173's own named hazard: (1) per-version capability isolation -- confirm an in-flight invocation of a superseded module version genuinely keeps THAT version's capability set (derived from that version's own immutable manifest snapshot, checked out at invocation start) even after activate/2 has installed a new version whose manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set; confirm there is no code path where a checked-out invocation's capability table could be re-derived from the CURRENT (post-activation) manifest instead of its own snapshot's; (2) the checkout mechanism -- confirm the version_snapshot() genuinely crosses the GenServer.call boundary as an immutable copy (BEAM process isolation), so no later mutation of the registry's internal state can reach back into an in-flight invocation's already-checked-out snapshot; (3) reference counting -- confirm the ref-count/release logic cannot be manipulated by guest-controlled input to prematurely release a version still in use, or to pin/leak a version forever; (4) the Process.monitor/:DOWN crash-safety mechanism -- confirm it correctly decrements the ref count for a genuinely hung, brutal-killed invocation without a race that could double-decrement or under-decrement; (5) confirm no host function or registry operation calls Letflow.Repo (or similar tenant-scoped resource) with a prefix or identifier derived from guest-supplied input; (6) confirm the new supervision-tree wiring in application.ex doesn't introduce a startup-order hazard or expose the registry process under a name a guest could somehow reach.
acceptance_criteria: a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time
